name: Learning Through Trial and Error
gist: Papers about training agents to get better by trying things, getting feedback, and adjusting their strategy — reinforcement learning for tool use.
explain: The core idea here is that agents learn by doing. You give the agent a task, it tries something, gets feedback on how well it worked, and adjusts its strategy next time. This is reinforcement learning — the agent gets rewarded for good moves and punished (or gets nothing) for bad ones. Over time, it figures out patterns: 'oh, when the problem looks like this, calling that tool first usually works' or 'I should check my answer before declaring victory'. The agent doesn't need to be explicitly programmed for every situation; it learns from experience.

The challenge is that reinforcement learning is slow and fragile. If an agent tries random things, it wastes a lot of time on bad moves before finding anything that works. A single mistake (like calling the wrong tool) can send it down the wrong path, and it has to learn that the hard way. Real-world tools also give messy feedback — sometimes they fail silently, sometimes they return confusing errors, sometimes they work but give unexpected results. The agent has to learn to interpret all of that and adjust. And if you change the tools even slightly or give it a new type of problem, it might have to relearn from scratch.

Papers in this area work on making that learning faster and more reliable, because waiting weeks for an agent to learn is impractical and random exploration wastes compute. Some focus on designing rewards so the agent gets useful feedback at each step, not just at the end, which means the agent knows sooner when it is on the right track. Others work on better algorithms that learn from fewer trials so agents don't have to try thousands of bad ideas before finding good ones. Some papers explore how agents can reuse knowledge from one set of tools to bootstrap learning on new tools, so they don't start from zero every time — that matters because most real problems use similar tools, and an agent that can transfer what it learned saves training time. The goal is to make learning practical enough that you can train an agent in reasonable time and have it actually become reliable.

papers.title: SEAgent: Self-Evolving Computer Use Agent with Autonomous Learning from Experience
papers.contribution: Achieves performance surpassing ensembles of specialist agents on their specialized software, validated on OSWorld, ScienceBoard, and AndroidWorld.

papers.title: Safe and Scalable Web Agent Learning via Recreated Websites
papers.contribution: Agents trained on VeriEnv generalize to unseen websites, achieve site-specific mastery through self-evolving training, and benefit from scaling training environments.

papers.title: Scalable Traffic Signal Control with Shared Policy Framework
papers.contribution: Maintains performance gains as network scale increases and outperforms rule-based, RL, and grouping-based baselines on real-world and synthetic networks.

papers.title: ScaleEnv: Scaling Environment Synthesis from Scratch for Generalist Interactive Tool-Use Agent Training
papers.contribution: Demonstrates significant performance improvements on unseen multi-turn tool-use benchmarks with empirical evidence that scaling environmental diversity is critical for robust agent learning.

papers.title: Scaling Agents via Continual Pre-training
papers.contribution: AgentFounder-30B achieves state-of-the-art on benchmarks including 39.9% BrowseComp-en, 43.3% BrowseComp-zh, and 31.5% HLE Pass@1 while retaining strong tool-use ability.

papers.title: Scaling Long-Horizon Agent via Context Folding
papers.contribution: Matches baseline performance on long-horizon tasks while using 10x smaller active context and outperforms models constrained to the same context size.

papers.title: Search Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of Agent Capability without Supervision
papers.contribution: Enables self-play agentic RLVR without supervision; proposer and solver co-evolve capabilities through competition and cooperation.

papers.title: SpatialReward: Bridging the Perception Gap in Online RL for Image Editing via Explicit Spatial Reasoning
papers.contribution: SpatialReward achieves state-of-the-art performance on MMRB2 and EditReward-Bench, outperforms proprietary evaluators, and boosts online RL by +0.90 on GEdit-Bench.

papers.title: Strategy-Aware Optimization Modeling with Reasoning LLMs
papers.contribution: Improves pass@1 from 72.7 to 80.3; pass@16 discovers 19-29% more distinct formulations with 14.2% fewer constraints than baseline for more solver-efficient modeling.

papers.title: Stream RAG: Instant and Accurate Spoken Dialogue Systems with Streaming Tool Usage
papers.contribution: Improves QA accuracy by over 20.0% absolute on AudioCRAG and achieves state-of-the-art on SLUE-SQA, while reducing latency by up to 57% relative to cascaded systems.

papers.title: Stronger-MAS: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative LLMs
papers.contribution: On long-horizon planning tasks, AT-GRPO boosts accuracy from 14.0-47.0% single-agent baseline to 96.0-99.5%, with average gains of 3.87-7.62% on coding and 9.0-17.93% on math.

papers.title: TRIP-Bench: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Interactive Agents in Real-World Scenarios
papers.contribution: Even advanced models achieve at most 50% on easy split; GTPO improves constraint satisfaction and robustness in Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct.

papers.title: The Value of Variance: Mitigating Debate Collapse in Multi-Agent Systems via Uncertainty-Driven Policy Optimization
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that calibrating multi-agent systems via uncertainty metrics reliably improves decision accuracy and reduces system disagreement in debate settings.

papers.title: Think Less, Act Early: Reinforced Latent Reasoning with Early Exit in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.contribution: Significantly reduces inference latency while achieving superior stability and success rates compared to full-reasoning baselines.

papers.title: ThunderAgent: A Fast, Simple, and Program-Aware Agentic Inference System
papers.contribution: Achieves 1.5-3.6x throughput improvements in serving, 1.8-3.9x in RL rollout, and up to 4.2x disk memory savings over state-of-the-art systems.

papers.title: TodoEvolve: Learning to Architect Agent Planning Systems
papers.contribution: Consistently surpasses engineered planning modules across five agentic benchmarks while maintaining economical API costs and runtime overhead.

papers.title: Toward Training Superintelligent Software Agents through Self-Play SWE-RL
papers.contribution: Achieves +10.4 and +7.8 point self-improvement on SWE-bench benchmarks, generalizing to unseen bug descriptions.

papers.title: Towards High-Fidelity CAD Generation via LLM-Driven Program Generation and Text-Based B-Rep Primitive Grounding
papers.contribution: FutureCAD achieves state-of-the-art CAD generation performance on new real-world CAD model dataset.

papers.title: Towards Pareto-Optimal Tool-Integrated Agents with Pareto Ranking Policy Optimization
papers.contribution: ParetoPO discovers policies with superior accuracy-efficiency trade-offs compared to static and heuristic baselines on mathematical reasoning and multi-hop QA.

papers.title: Towards Persistent Noise-Tolerant Active Learning of Regular Languages with Class Query
papers.contribution: Augmented L* loop with class queries enables DFA learning under persistent noise without demonstrations.

papers.title: Trade in Minutes! Rationality-Driven Agentic System for Quantitative Financial Trading
papers.contribution: Demonstrates stable profitability across 200+ trading pairs with efficient action selection and risk control under volatile market dynamics.

papers.title: Training LLM Agents to Empower Humans
papers.contribution: User study shows participants preferred the empowerment assistant 78% of the time with 31% higher acceptance rate, providing aligned AI agents without human feedback or verifiable rewards.

papers.title: Training Language Model Agents to Find Vulnerabilities with CTF-Dojo
papers.contribution: LLM agents achieve up to 11.6% absolute gains over strong baselines on three competitive benchmarks, with the best 32B model reaching 31.9% Pass@1, rivaling frontier models.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Clarification in LLM Agents with Information Gain
papers.contribution: Improves success rate by 3.7% over no-clarification baseline while adding only 0.3 average interaction steps, with cross-agent evaluation across five backbones.

papers.title: Unlocking Long-Horizon Agentic Search with Large-Scale End-to-End RL
papers.contribution: ASearcher achieves GAIA 58.1, xBench 51.1, and Frames 74.5 using only basic search tools, with further improvements to 71.8, 75.0, and 83.4 using zero-shot enhancements.

papers.title: VeriRole: Verifiable Role-Awareness through Hint-Guided Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves 18.9% improvement on RAIDEN and 4.55% on CharacterEval benchmarks for role-aware persona consistency.

papers.title: VideoAgentTrek: Computer-Use Pretraining from Unlabeled Videos
papers.contribution: From 39,000 YouTube videos generates 1.52 million interaction steps; improves OSWorld-Verified success from 9.3% to 15.8% (70% relative gain) and AgentNetBench step accuracy from 64.1% to 69.3%.

papers.title: VideoZoomer: Reinforcement-Learned Temporal Focusing for Long Video Reasoning
papers.contribution: A 7B model demonstrates diverse reasoning patterns consistently surpassing open-source models and rivaling proprietary systems on long video understanding benchmarks.

papers.title: WebFactory: Automated Compression of Foundational Language Intelligence into Grounded Web Agents
papers.contribution: Agent trained on synthetic data from 10 websites achieves performance comparable to agents trained on same human-annotated data from much larger environments.

papers.title: WebGen-Agent: Enhancing Interactive Website Generation with Multi-Level Feedback and Step-Level Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Increases Claude 3.5 Sonnet's accuracy from 26.4% to 51.9% on WebGen-Bench with improved appearance scores, outperforming state-of-the-art agents.

papers.title: WebSailor-V2: Bridging the Chasm to Proprietary Agents via Synthetic Data and Scalable Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Qwen3-30B-A3B agent achieves 35.3 BrowseComp-EN, 44.1 BrowseComp-ZH, 30.6 HLE, surpassing DeepSeek-V3.1 and competing with proprietary systems.

papers.title: WebSeer: Training Deeper Search Agents through Reinforcement Learning with Self-Reflection
papers.contribution: Using a single 14B model, achieves state-of-the-art results on HotpotQA (72.3% accuracy) and SimpleQA (90.0% accuracy) with strong generalization to out-of-distribution datasets.
